meta.title: AI image generation prompts – Blue Wildebeest, Greater Kudu, Impala, Gemsbok
meta.purpose: Limpopo game reserve, MIWESU. Natural, beautiful shots only. No hunters, no weapons, no blood, no mutilation.
meta.location: Limpopo province, South Africa – Makoppa district / Waterberg region
meta.terrain: Flat to gently undulating. No mountains, no dramatic peaks or cliffs in frame.

vegetation_reference.description: Limpopo bushveld / Arid Sweet Bushveld – use for all backgrounds
vegetation_reference.ground: Red to reddish-brown soil (Hutton-type, iron-rich). Fine, powdery; can show hoof prints. Short to medium sweetveld grasses, dry season: pale straw-yellow or ash-grey; wet season: green.
vegetation_reference.trees_shrubs: Mopane (Colophospermum mopane) – butterfly-shaped leaves, copper/yellow in dry season; Sicklebush (Dichrostachys cinerea); Acacia (e.g. umbrella thorn, blackthorn) – thorny, often flat-topped; Leadwood (Combretum); Grewia. Sparse to moderate canopy, not dense forest.
vegetation_reference.lighting: Golden hour (dawn/dusk) or soft overcast; harsh midday OK for some scenes. Dust in dry season can create warm, saturated light.
vegetation_reference.forbidden: Mountains, snow, tropical rainforest, desert dunes, European woodland, people, vehicles, fences, buildings, hunting, blood, wounded or dead animals.

species.key_traits: Large, front-heavy; slate-grey to bluish-grey coat with silvery sheen in sun; dark vertical stripes (brindled); jet-black forehead and face in mature bull, chestnut-brown forehead in cow; short stiff black mane; shaggy black beard; horse-like long black tail; horns curve out then up and in (both sexes), heavy boss in bulls.

species.key_traits: Large spiral-horned antelope. Bull: slate-grey to bluish-grey, 6–10 vertical white stripes, white facial chevron, throat beard, massive spiral horns (2.5 twists). Cow: tawny/reddish-brown/cinnamon, no horns, smaller. Large ears, white tail underside (flag).

species.key_traits: Medium antelope. Reddish-brown dorsal saddle, pale fawn flanks, white underbelly. Black M-marking on rump, black stripe down tail, black ear tips, black tufts above heels. Only male has lyre-shaped ridged horns.

species.key_traits: Large, heavy-fronted. Fawn-grey/sandy-tan coat, white underbelly. Stark white face with black warpaint: inverted triangle on nose/forehead, broad black stripes from horn base over eyes to jaw, black chin-to-chest stripe. Thick black horizontal band on flanks; white legs with black patches above knees/hocks. Long straight horns (both sexes): heavily annulated lower 2/3, smooth sharp tip. Male horns thicker shorter (83–96 cm), female longer thinner (96–120 cm). Short stiff black dorsal mane. Long black brush tail.

Two or three gemsbok in flat open bushveld, red soil, grass, scattered Mopane or knob thorn. Limpopo South Africa, wide shot, golden hour or overcast. Photorealistic, no people, no mountains.
Single gemsbok in dappled shade under Acacia or Mopane scrub, black-and-white face and fawn body visible. Flat bushveld, red/grey soil. Limpopo, photorealistic, no mountains.
